# Superpower (health membership: labs, imaging, longevity coaching)

URL: https://superpower.com/ — Awwwards Site of the Day, designed by Daybreak Studio

## Type system
- Display/body: `"Nb international pro webfont", Arial, sans-serif` used at
  every level — H1 56.2px/400, H2 37.5px/400, body/button 15px/400. A
  single grotesk family, weight kept at regular throughout (hierarchy comes
  from size and colour, not boldness), giving the page a cool, technical
  evenness.

## Color system
- bg: white `#FFFFFF` and near-white `#FAFAFA`.
- accent: burnt orange `#FC5F2B`, applied specifically to icon/illustration
  strokes rather than large fills or button backgrounds — a restrained use
  of a genuinely warm, high-energy colour.
- Overlay/scrim blacks at multiple opacities (`rgba(0,0,0,0.5)`,
  `rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`) used on photographic hero sections for text legibility.
- Neutral grey `#E2E2E2` for dividers/secondary surfaces.
- Hero photography itself is warm/backlit (amber glow) even though the UI
  chrome is white — the "dark/high-tech" mood comes from photography and
  device-mockup styling, not from a dark page background.

## Layout & grid
- Full-bleed backlit-amber hero photo (a person in silhouette) with white
  UI overlaid — headline top-left, small CTA.
- "How it works" section uses three tall image cards (test kit, results
  screen, protocol) in a horizontal row.
- A large, centred iPad/tablet mockup showing the live product dashboard
  (charts, biomarker rings) is the visual anchor of the page, floating over
  generous whitespace — the single largest compositional element on the
  page besides the hero.
- Long vertical whitespace gaps between sections (the full-page screenshot
  shows extensive blank space), giving a slow, confident pacing typical of
  premium product sites.

## Sections (order observed)
1. Full-bleed amber-lit photographic hero, "Your new health membership,"
   CTA
2. Press/partner logo strip
3. "How it works" — 3-step image card row (test based on biology, results
   explained, build protocol, track everything)
4. Large product-dashboard tablet mockup with a person holding/reviewing it
   — "Every membership starts with 100+ biomarkers"
5. Price-anchor callout: "What could cost $10,000 is now $199"
6. "Led by doctors with 40 years of health and longevity expertise" —
   advisor headshot row
7. "Changing outcomes and lives across the nation" — two large lifestyle
   photos with testimonial captions
8. "Used by athletes, doctors, and members just like you" — social-proof
   photo grid with phone screenshot
9. Membership pricing card ("$199, starts here")
10. Closing amber-lit hero repeat ("Health is your superpower")
11. Footer

## Components/signature
- The floating tablet/device mockup showing the actual product dashboard
  (biomarker rings, charts) mid-page is the site's signature device — it
  makes the abstract promise of "100+ biomarkers" concrete without
  requiring the marketing page itself to render real data tables.
- Restrained orange used only on line-art icons/illustrations, never as a
  background fill — keeps the page reading clean/white while still having
  a distinct warm identity colour.

## Motion/interactions
- Awwwards citation notes scrolling transitions, 3D effects and
  microinteractions — consistent with the floating device mockup likely
  having scroll-linked parallax/rotation.

## Biomarker/trust presentation
- Biomarker data is shown via a product-dashboard mockup (rings/charts
  inside a device frame) rather than embedded directly in the marketing
  page — keeps the page light while still visually promising a data-rich
  product.
- Trust: doctor advisor headshots with tenure claim ("40 years of health
  and longevity expertise"), athlete/member social proof photography, and
  a price-anchor comparison ("$10,000 → $199") rather than a feature
  comparison table.

## What works
- Demonstrates the "dark/high-tech" mood can be achieved on a white-background
  site purely through warm, backlit photography and a floating device
  mockup — proves this cluster doesn't require literal dark-mode UI.
- Single-family, single-weight typography paired with one restrained accent
  colour reads confident and engineered rather than corporate.

## Avoid
- Extremely long whitespace gaps between sections (visible in the
  full-page capture) risk feeling sparse on a slower connection or smaller
  viewport — tighten vertical rhythm if content density is a priority.
- Orange-only-on-icons is a subtle move that can get lost if the accent
  isn't reinforced elsewhere (e.g., in the product UI itself).

## How to apply
- Use warm, backlit/golden-hour photography plus a single desaturated
  accent restricted to icon strokes to achieve a "premium tech" mood
  without a literal dark background.
- Anchor a mid-page section with a large floating device mockup showing
  the real product UI (charts/rings) as proof of data depth, instead of
  building out biomarker tables directly in the marketing page.
